creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Typing in the devenv window lags 100-250 ms with three Claude Code agents working, on a 2 ms link, with the box 92% idle. The time goes into herdr. Its main thread does a full virtual render of every attached client on each pass and answers API requests from the same thread, so a keystroke waits for whatever render is in flight. Muster keeps a client attached to every pane in the window, including the ones behind other tabs, so herdr renders seven panes nobody can see.

## What was measured

2026-09-04, muster 0.6.0, herdr 0.8.0, ten panes in four tabs on the devenv, three agents `working`:

    herdr main thread: 53-68% of one core, sustained (/proc/<pid>/task/<pid>/stat, 5 s samples)
    the laptop's herdr, two panes, one Claude Code: 13-16% of a core
    pane.send_input round trip (server_channel.sent, ms): n=84, median 120, p90 178, max 249
    herdr pane.focus, server side: 33-45 ms while busy, 1-12 ms when quiet
    ping to the box: 2.0 ms; ssh -O check on the master: 20 ms

The round trips were logged 15:48 to 16:15 and overlap the oversized-frame episode in the frozen-pane card for 16 of those minutes, but the first samples, before it began, were already 126-147 ms.

`perf record -g -p <herdr>` over 4 s, self time:

    10.6%  alloc::vec::Vec::extend_with
    10.2%  ghostty_render_state_row_cells_get
     8.4%  malloc + free
     3.8%  Vec::clone
     3.0%  herdr::pane::terminal::PaneTerminal::render
     2.9%  ratatui_core::buffer::Buffer::diff
     2.1%  herdr::protocol::wire::FrameData::from_ratatui_buffer_with_hyperlinks

The loop is `src/server/headless.rs` near line 4100: for each attached client, `render_terminal_virtual(runtime, area)`, `visible_hyperlinks`, `FrameData::from_ratatui_buffer_with_hyperlinks`, serialize. Allocation leads, which says the buffers are rebuilt each pass rather than reused.

Hidden panes were rendered like visible ones. Between 16:05 and 16:15 the INVESTIGATIONS tab was on screen for about 40 seconds, and its bridge w4:pE received 0.65 frames per second throughout. `muster window --json` at 16:15: 10 panes attached, 3 `on_screen`.

## What Muster can do

- Stop paying for hidden panes. A pane behind another tab needs its state and its scrollback, not a frame per change. Detaching the control client and reattaching on show (`--takeover`, which the bridge already uses to replace a predecessor) is one shape; a lower render rate is another, and herdr does not offer one today. Seven idle clients of ten would have more than halved the daemon's load here.
- Keep the number. `server_channel.sent` carries `ms` because `a_26BIX28HG` routed keys that way on the number being small. A record with impact and check fields when the median crosses, say, 50 ms turns the next occurrence into one line instead of a profiling session.

## Upstream

The per-pass allocation and the single render thread are herdr's (herdrdev/herdr). docs/origin.md:85 says daemon-side gaps become upstream PRs; this is one. Attach the profile above, and ask separately whether API requests can be answered off the render thread, which is what turns a slow render into slow typing.
title: 🐢 herdr renders every attached pane in full on one thread, and typing waits behind it
